We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available precursors). The target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-one?). Actually structure: methyl ester attached to a bicyclic [C@]12... It's likely methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate? Let's decode: COC(=O) attached to a chiral carbon bridging two rings. So maybe it's methyl (1R,2S)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate? The bicyclic core is a decalin with a carbonyl at bridgehead? Actually C(C2)=O indicates a ketone on the other ring.

Thus target could be synthesized via Diels-Alder of a diene and a dienophile then oxidation/esterification. But only 1 step allowed, so we need a single reaction that directly forms the product from two commercially available precursors. Could be a Michael addition? But need to match template.

We have a template from search result id 1914385 which seems to be a retro-DA: product is our target, reactants are a diene (CH2=CH-CH=CH2) and a methyl ester of a cyclohexenone? Let's examine reactant_smiles from that entry: '[CH2:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH2:9].[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1'

First reactant: CH2=CH-CH=CH2 (1,3-butadiene). Second: methyl ester of a cyclohexenone? Let's decode: CH3O C(=O) C1=CH C(=O) CH2 1. That's methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one-4-carboxylate? Actually SMILES: COC(=O)C1=CHC(=O)CH2C1? Wait: [CH3][O][C](=O)[C]1=[CH][C](=O)[CH2]1. That's methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate? This seems plausible and likely commercially available.

Thus the retro-DA template suggests forward reaction: Diels-Alder between a diene (butadiene) and a dienophile (the methyl cyclohexenone ester) to give the bicyclic product (our target). That is a single step reaction (thermal Diels-Alder). Both precursors are commercially available: 1,3-butadiene (gas) maybe not typical but can be purchased as solution; methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one-4-carboxylate? Might be less common. Let's check buyability of that second SMILES: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)C=CC1"? Actually we need the exact SMILES from template: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)C=CC1"? Wait the reactant SMILES: [CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1. That is COC(=O)C1=CHC(=O)CH2C1. Let's generate a SMILES: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)CC1"? Not exactly. Let's construct: COC(=O)C1=CHC(=O)CH2C1. Write: "COC(=O)C1=CHC(=O)C H2 C1"? The CH2 is part of ring. So SMILES: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)CC1"? That would be methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate? Let's test buyability of "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)CC1".
